study_identification_part.si_4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange) dataset was used, containing structural MRI data from 20 independent samples collected at 17 different scanning locations. The dataset includes 569 healthy controls (after outlier correction from original 573) and 482 individuals with autism spectrum disorder.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The ABIDE consortium (http://preprocessed-connectomesproject.org/abide/) was founded to facilitate research and collaboration on autism spectrum disorders by data aggregation and sharing. The consortium provides a publicly available structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data set and corresponding phenotypic information of 539 individuals with autism spectrum disorder and 573 age-matched typical controls. For this study, we used 569 controls for development and performance testing of the models, out of which 470 were male.

answer.ABIDE (autism sample): clinical validation to test model's ability to retain clinically useful information while removing site effects

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The healthy control sample (n=569) was split into training set (70%, n=389) and test set (30%, n=166) using within-site split while preserving age, sex, and site distribution. The autism sample (n=482) was used separately to validate whether the hierarchical Bayesian models retain clinically useful variance while correcting for site effects.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: For this study, we used 569 controls for development and performance testing of the models... In a subsequent step, we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set... To evaluate the performance of the models, we split the the healthy control data set into a training set (70% of data, n=389) and a test set (30% of data, n=166)...

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: Age statistics are provided separately for males and females in controls: Male (n=470): M=17.5, SD=8.3; Female (n=99): M=15.6, SD=7.0. Overall range: 6.5-40 years. Weighted mean calculated as (470*17.5 + 99*15.6)/569 = 17.18. Pooled SD calculated as sqrt[((470-1)*8.3^2 + (99-1)*7.0^2)/(470+99-2)] = 8.02. Training and test sets preserved age distribution but specific train-phase statistics not reported.
